narrative:
The model estimates an 81% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who eventually depart.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook, in order of importance, were the availability of other job opportunities, your overall years of experience, and your monthly salary level. 

Having received other job offers while at the company was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay (77%) report receiving no external offers, so this stands out as a clear signal of outside interest that often precedes departure. Your six to ten years of total professional experience also contributed to the “will leave” direction; while this is a fairly common range, it is less typical among those predicted to stay, where half have only one to five years. Finally, your salary in the 11k–15k SAR range added further weight toward leaving. This bracket is relatively uncommon among employees the model sees as likely to remain, most of whom earn either 6k–10k or 1k–5k.

Taken together, these elements suggest you may be in a strong position to explore new roles. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, while you may wish to openly evaluate whether your current path still meets your long-term goals. (218 words)
